briefing.headline: UK and US political tensions rise as parties confront internal challenges
briefing.overview: Britain sees debate over devolution and party extremism, while the US Justice Department faces scrutiny over media investigations. Both systems grapple with how institutions balance power and accountability.

stories.title: DUP claims power to oust Northern Ireland First Minister
stories.what_happened: Carla Lockhart of the DUP said unionist voters are angry with First Minister Michelle O'Neill over the Garvaghy Road protests. She argued that the DUP could use its position to remove O'Neill from office.
stories.why_it_matters: The claim highlights the fragility of power‑sharing arrangements under the Good Friday Agreement, a key element of the UK constitution. It shows how devolution can create contested executive authority.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Unionists say the move protects community interests and enforces accountability.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Nationalists warn it could destabilise the power‑sharing institutions and breach the peace process.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives view it as a legitimate use of parliamentary procedure.

key_term.definition: The transfer of powers from the central UK government to regional bodies such as the Scottish Parliament or Northern Ireland Assembly.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence in an essay on the strengths and weaknesses of the UK’s devolved constitution.

stories.title: Green MP warns against extremist capture of party
stories.what_happened: A Green Party MP said the party must guard against being captured by extremists and racists. The comment came amid internal disputes over party policy and leadership.
stories.why_it_matters: The issue illustrates intra‑party democracy and the tension between broad membership bases and ideological control, a core topic in the AQA study of political parties.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Party members say vigilance protects the Greens’ progressive values.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents claim the warning may be used to silence dissenting voices within the party.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive activists stress the need for inclusive decision‑making.

key_term.definition: The internal processes by which party members influence policy, leadership and candidate selection.

stories.exam_use: Cite when discussing the advantages and disadvantages of internal party democracy.

stories.title: Justice Department probes TV networks for antitrust concerns
stories.what_happened: The US Justice Department opened an investigation into several television networks for possible antitrust violations. The probe follows ongoing disputes between the Trump administration and the press.
stories.why_it_matters: The case shows how US courts can check corporate power and how the executive branch may use legal mechanisms to influence media, linking to the AQA focus on the US courts and separation of powers.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Proponents say the investigation protects competition and consumer choice.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Critics claim it is a politically motivated attack on press freedom.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives view it as a necessary enforcement of antitrust law.

key_term.definition: Legislation designed to prevent monopolies and promote competition.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence when evaluating the role of US courts in regulating corporate behaviour.

stories.title: Trump and Vance campaign intensify in Ohio
stories.what_happened: Former President Donald Trump and Vice‑presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy are campaigning heavily in Ohio ahead of the mid‑term elections. Polls show Democrat Amy Acton narrowing the gap.
stories.why_it_matters: The race illustrates US party competition, candidate strategy and the impact of national figures on state elections, all covered in the AQA syllabus on parties and elections.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Republicans say the high‑profile visits energise the base and highlight policy successes.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Democrats argue the focus on personalities distracts from local issues.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressives warn the campaign may polarise voters further.

key_term.definition: Elections held halfway through a president’s four‑year term, often determining control of Congress.

stories.exam_use: Reference when discussing how party leadership influences electoral outcomes.

stories.title: UK climate‑action debate at party conferences
stories.what_happened: During the party conference season, the Conservatives announced plans to scrap low‑carbon housebuilding, the Greens backed new nuclear reactors, and Labour paused oil‑drilling decisions. Commentators called for less point‑scoring politics.
stories.why_it_matters: The differing policy positions show how parties compete on environmental issues, linking to the AQA theme of parties and pressure groups influencing policy.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Conservatives claim scrapping the policy reduces costs for developers.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Environmental groups say it undermines climate targets.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Right‑leaning analysts argue market‑driven solutions are preferable.

key_term.definition: The set of proposals a party promises to implement if elected.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate how parties differentiate themselves on climate policy.

compare.uk: UK parties such as the Greens and Conservatives compete over climate policy, with internal debates about ideological direction and member control.
compare.us: US parties contest elections through high‑profile candidate campaigns, with national figures shaping state races like Ohio’s governor’s race.
compare.insight: The contrast shows UK parties often focus on policy detail within parliamentary systems, while US parties rely more on charismatic leaders and electoral mobilisation.

ideas_lens.text: The Justice Department’s antitrust probe reflects liberalism’s emphasis on limiting corporate power and protecting individual choice, echoing John Stuart Mill’s arguments for competition. Liberal thinkers also stress the importance of an independent judiciary to enforce these principles.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which internal party democracy influences policy outcomes in the UK and the US.
exam_question.tip: Compare a UK party’s internal debate (e.g., Green Party) with US party candidate strategy (e.g., Trump’s Ohio campaign) and link each to the concept of party democracy.
